method_card.title: TV, Film and Streaming
steps: Learn the key vocabulary for TV programmes, film genres and streaming
Master the perfect tense with avoir to talk about films you have watched
Use opinion phrases with adjective agreement to give your views
Build sentences combining past experiences with opinions and comparatives
method_card.content:
This lesson covers TV and film vocabulary, streaming habits, and how to use the perfect tense with avoir and opinion phrases in the context of media.

FrenchEnglish
un film d'actionan action film
une comédiea comedy
un film d'horreura horror film
un film de science-fictiona science-fiction film
un documentairea documentary
une sériea series
une émissiona programme
la chaînethe TV channel
regarder en streamingto watch by streaming
téléchargerto download
le dessin animéthe cartoon / animated film
le journal téléviséthe TV news
un acteur / une actricean actor / an actress
passionnant(e)exciting / gripping
ennuyeux / ennuyeuseboring

Perfect tense with avoir: For most verbs, use avoir + past participle. The past participle of regular -er verbs ends in -é: regarder → regardé. Irregular: voir → vu, lire → lu, prendre → pris. Example: J'ai regardé une série ce soir. (I watched a series this evening.) Nous avons vu un film d'action. (We watched an action film.)

Opinion phrases: Je pense que c'est / c'était + adjective. Remember adjectives must agree: un film ennuyeux (m sg) but une émission ennuyeuse (f sg). Je trouve que + sentence. À mon avis = in my opinion.

Model paragraph: Hier soir, j'ai regardé une série policière en streaming. C'était très passionnant et les acteurs étaient excellents. Je préfère regarder des films d'action parce qu'ils sont plus excitants que les documentaires. (Last night I watched a crime series on streaming. It was very exciting and the actors were excellent. I prefer watching action films because they are more exciting than documentaries.)

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — media and technology appears across all papers

worked_examples.question: Translate to English: 'Hier soir, j'ai regardé un film d'action avec mon frère. C'était très passionnant.'

steps.label: Break it down
steps.content: Hier soir | j'ai regardé | un film d'action | avec mon frère | C'était très passionnant.

steps.label: Identify the tenses
steps.content: j'ai regardé = I watched (perfect tense: avoir + past participle regardé). C'était = It was (imperfect — used for descriptions in the past).

steps.label: Translate the key items
steps.content: un film d'action = an action film. passionnant = exciting / gripping. No adjective agreement needed here as it follows c'était and is masculine singular by default.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Last night, I watched an action film with my brother. It was very exciting.

worked_examples.question: How do you make adjectives agree with feminine nouns? Give an example using 'ennuyeux'.

steps.label: Check the noun's gender
steps.content: Find the noun you are describing. Is it masculine or feminine? Un film = masculine. Une émission = feminine.

steps.label: Apply the agreement rule
steps.content: Adjectives ending in -eux change to -euse in the feminine: ennuyeux → ennuyeuse. So: un film ennuyeux (m) but une émission ennuyeuse (f).

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Always match the adjective ending to the gender of the noun. Ce film est ennuyeux. (m) — Cette série est ennuyeuse. (f)

bronze.question: Match the French TV and film words to the English meaning
Match the French verbs and adjectives to the English meaning
Complete the sentence with the correct perfect tense form
sentence_parts: un film d'horreur hier soir. C'

gaps.correct_explain: ai regardé is the perfect tense of regarder: avoir (ai) + past participle (regardé).

wrong.regardé: regardé alone is just the past participle — you need avoir first: ai regardé.
wrong.ai regarder: regarder is the infinitive, not the past participle. Use regardé after ai.

gaps.correct_explain: était is the imperfect of être used with c' to describe something in the past: c'était = it was.

wrong.est: est is the present tense. The sentence is in the past (yesterday), so you need the imperfect: était.
wrong.a été: a été is the perfect tense — for descriptions in the past, French uses the imperfect: c'était.

bronze.question: Complete the sentence with the correct adjective form
sentence_parts: Je préfère les comédies car elles sont

gaps.correct_explain: drôles agrees with elles (= les comédies, feminine plural). Drôle adds -s for plural.

wrong.drôle: drôle is singular. Les comédies is plural — add -s: drôles.
wrong.drôleux: drôleux is not a real word. The plural of drôle is simply drôles.

gaps.correct_explain: effrayants agrees with les films d'horreur (masculine plural). Add -s to the masculine form.

wrong.effrayant: effrayant is singular. Les films is plural — add -s: effrayants.
wrong.effrayante: effrayante is the feminine singular form. Film is masculine — use effrayant / effrayants.

bronze.question: What does 'Je regarde souvent des séries en streaming le week-end' mean?
options: I often watch series on streaming at the weekend
I sometimes download series at the weekend
I watched a series on TV last weekend
I never watch TV at the weekend

bronze.question: Which sentence correctly uses the perfect tense to say 'We watched a documentary'?

model_answers: In the evening, I watch a cookery programme with my family. My favourite series is a French comedy.
In the evening, I watch a cooking programme with my family. My favourite series is a French comedy.
hints: une émission de cuisine = a cookery programme
ma série préférée = my favourite series

silver.question: Complete the sentence by typing the correct word
silver.english: We saw a comedy at the cinema last Saturday. It was very funny.
sentence_parts: une comédie au cinéma samedi dernier. C'était très

gaps.correct_explain: avons vu is the perfect tense of voir: avoir (avons) + irregular past participle vu.

wrong.avons voir: voir is the infinitive. After avons you need the past participle: vu.
wrong.sommes vu: voir uses avoir as auxiliary, not être. Use avons vu.

gaps.correct_explain: drôle does not change for gender or number — it is the same for all nouns: c'était drôle.

wrong.drôles: drôles is plural. Here c'était refers to a single comedy, so use the singular: drôle.

silver.question: Find and fix the grammatical error
silver.explanation: série is feminine (une série), so the adjective must be in the feminine form: ennuyeux → ennuyeuse (change -eux to -euse).

silver.question: Build the sentence in French
silver.english: I watched a crime series on streaming last night.

distractor_labels.regarder: wrong form — after avoir (j'ai) you need the past participle regardé, not the infinitive regarder

silver.source_text: I watched a documentary on TV. It was interesting.
model_answers: J'ai regardé un documentaire à la télé. C'était intéressant.
J'ai regardé un documentaire à la télévision. C'était intéressant.

gold.question: Build the sentence in French
gold.english: The actress who played in this film is very well known.

distractor_labels.connu: wrong agreement — actrice is feminine, so the adjective must be connue (with -e), not connu
distractor_labels.qu': wrong relative pronoun — qui is used for the subject of the clause (she played), que is for the object
distractor_labels.joue: wrong tense — the action happened in the past, so use the perfect tense: a joué

gold.question: Role Play
gold.scenario: You are at a cinema with a French friend. You are talking to the person at the ticket desk. The setting is a cinema / theatre / concert hall.

bullets.prompt: Greet the ticket assistant and ask for two tickets for the 7 o'clock showing.
bullets.model_answer: Bonjour ! Je voudrais deux billets pour la séance de dix-neuf heures, s'il vous plaît.
bullets.note: je voudrais (polite conditional) + deux billets + pour la séance de + time

bullets.prompt: Ask what kind of film it is and say you prefer comedies.
bullets.model_answer: C'est quel genre de film ? Je préfère les comédies.
bullets.note: quel genre de film ? (what type of film?) + je préfère + definite article (les comédies)

bullets.prompt: Say that you watched a horror film last week and it was very frightening.
bullets.model_answer: La semaine dernière, j'ai regardé un film d'horreur et c'était très effrayant.
bullets.note: la semaine dernière + perfect tense (j'ai regardé) + imperfect description (c'était)

bullets.prompt: Ask if there is a snack bar and say you would like to buy some popcorn.
bullets.model_answer: Est-ce qu'il y a un bar à snacks ? Je voudrais acheter du popcorn.
bullets.note: est-ce qu'il y a + je voudrais acheter + partitive du

gold.question: Complete the sentence by typing the correct word
gold.english: The film that we watched last night was better than the one we saw last week.
sentence_parts: nous avons regardé hier soir était meilleur
celui que nous avons vu la semaine dernière.

gaps.correct_explain: que (or qu' before a vowel) replaces the direct object of the clause. Here, nous avons regardé the film = the film is the object, so use que.

wrong.qui: qui is used for the subject of the clause (the thing doing the action). Here the film is the object (we watched it), so use que.

gaps.correct_explain: meilleur que = better than. The comparative structure in French is [adjective] + que.

wrong.de: meilleur de means 'the best of', not 'better than'. For comparisons use meilleur que.
